idea: Attach just enough gas that the MPC call/callback fails after state changed; check methods that skip need_gas (execute_upgrade, adopt_signature)
outcome: All MPC-reaching methods (agent_act,dao_act,advance,settle,probe,cancel,credit_deposit,guardian_unwind,execute->Outflow) go through need_gas(100 Tgas). execute_upgrade and adopt_signature skip need_gas but create NO MPC promise: adopt_signature only verifies in-contract and pushes a signed draft; execute_upgrade only runs on a DAO-approved upgrade (take_upgrade requires upgrade_ready==sha256(code)) and a panic rolls the whole call back atomically. Callback gas (GAS_CALLBACK=30T) is fixed by the contract, not caller-controlled; on OOG the callback reverts and state is retryable (sign_unknown / re-settle), never half-applied.
notes: No state-vs-callback inconsistency reachable by an attacker.

idea: Inflate trust.level/cap without a real MPC attestation, or avoid a required reset (reconcile, late proof, cancel-after-main, double-count)
outcome: count_proved_landing is called only from after_slot when status==Done && origin==Agent && EVERY slot is Landed{Main}. Landed{Main} is set only in on_verified's Main branch after check_attestation verifies the signature against foreign_pk (real MPC attestation). dao_resolve sets TrustedLanded (not Landed{Main}) so resolves never count. Double-count paths all closed: a second settle on a closed slot returns already_settled (no after_slot); reconcile_landed (Reverted->Main) adjusts only the ledger and never calls after_slot/count; a cancel cannot settle after a Main landing (slot not Open). All false-success closes (Cancel/Probe/dao_resolve false) are preceded by a reset_trust(OpIntervention) in the intervening method for agent ops. Migration (legacy.rs:173) sets last_change_epoch=current epoch and trust_floor=ceiling (neutral), preserving the per-step epoch wait.
notes: No trust inflation and no skipped reset found.

idea: Make preview_policy/preview_outflow disagree with propose_policy/dao_act across epoch rollover, pause, stale parked
outcome: preview_policy and propose_policy call the same policy::classify(current,new); dao_act rolls the epoch before computing fast-outflow left, and preview_outflow computes used=0 when now/epoch_ms != epoch.index, so both treat a rolled-over epoch as a fresh fast allowance (agree). preview reports paused/enough_idle as informational flags; the apply path enforces them as rejects. Stale-parked: preview is a current-policy snapshot; execute() re-checks classify(current,parked.policy)>lane -> StaleParked. No lane/wait divergence that would let a loosening apply as if FAST.
notes: Previews are consistent snapshots; no exploitable disagreement.

idea: Stored XSS / UI deception via on-chain data an outsider influences (account ids, reject reasons/details, event data, op fields, credit entries, verifying callers) rendered by web/
outcome: Every interpolation into innerHTML routes through esc() (escapes & < > " '), including reasonText/actionText outputs and the helpers (a(),pill() esc their inputs; stat()/kv() receive pre-esc'd vals). Independently, every on-chain field an outsider can set is charset-constrained so it cannot carry HTML metacharacters: NEAR account ids (Verifying.caller, rejection caller) are [a-z0-9._-]; guardian ids are base58 pubkeys; tx/hash/from are hex; amounts are numeric; Reject::WrongState/PolicyInvalid details are fixed contract literals (no attacker echo). No injectable field found.
notes: No live write performed: brief says to write to the arena only if an injectable field is found. None was.
